name: AWS - Well-Architected Framework
description: The six pillars of the AWS Well-Architected Framework: open a pillar to see its design principles

elements.description: Six pillars for designing and running reliable, secure, efficient, cost-effective, and sustainable workloads in the cloud
elements.label: AWS Well-Architected Framework

elements.description: Run and monitor systems to deliver business value, and keep improving the processes and procedures that support them
elements.label: Operational Excellence

elements.description: Protect data, systems, and assets, using cloud technologies to improve your security
elements.label: Security

elements.description: A workload performing its intended function correctly and consistently, whenever it's expected to
elements.label: Reliability

elements.description: Use computing resources efficiently to meet requirements, and stay efficient as demand and technologies change
elements.label: Performance Efficiency

elements.description: Run systems to deliver business value at the lowest price point
elements.label: Cost Optimization

elements.description: Minimise the environmental impacts of running cloud workloads
elements.label: Sustainability

name: AWS - Operational Excellence
description: The design principles of the Operational Excellence pillar of the AWS Well-Architected Framework

elements.description: Run and monitor systems to deliver business value, and keep improving the processes and procedures that support them
elements.label: Operational Excellence

elements.description: Align teams, leadership, and operating models to the outcomes the business needs
elements.label: Organize teams around business outcomes

elements.description: Understand how the workload behaves, performs, and is used, so you can act on it
elements.label: Implement observability for actionable insights

elements.description: Define the workload and its operations as code, with guardrails, to limit human error
elements.label: Safely automate where possible

elements.description: Small changes are easier to test and to undo, and reduce the scope of a failure
elements.label: Make frequent, small, reversible changes

elements.description: Keep runbooks current as the workload evolves, and rehearse them in game days
elements.label: Refine operations procedures frequently

elements.description: Run pre-mortems, test failure scenarios, and know how you'll respond
elements.label: Anticipate failure

elements.description: Share what you learn from events and failures across teams
elements.label: Learn from all operational events and metrics

elements.description: Let AWS run what it can, to reduce your operational burden
elements.label: Use managed services

name: AWS - Security
description: The design principles of the Security pillar of the AWS Well-Architected Framework

elements.description: Protect data, systems, and assets, using cloud technologies to improve your security
elements.label: Security

elements.description: Least privilege, separation of duties, centralised identity, and no long-term static credentials
elements.label: Implement a strong identity foundation

elements.description: Monitor, alert on, and audit actions and changes in real time
elements.label: Maintain traceability

elements.description: Defence in depth: the network edge, VPC, load balancing, every instance, OS, application, and code
elements.label: Apply security at all layers

elements.description: Security controls defined and managed as code, in version control
elements.label: Automate security best practices

elements.description: Classify data by sensitivity, and use encryption, tokenisation, and access control
elements.label: Protect data in transit and at rest

elements.description: Reduce direct access and manual processing of data with tools and automation
elements.label: Keep people away from data

elements.description: Have incident management processes, and run simulations to rehearse them
elements.label: Prepare for security events

name: AWS - Reliability
description: The design principles of the Reliability pillar of the AWS Well-Architected Framework

elements.description: A workload performing its intended function correctly and consistently, whenever it's expected to
elements.label: Reliability

elements.description: Monitor key performance indicators and trigger automation when a threshold is breached
elements.label: Automatically recover from failure

elements.description: Use automation to simulate failures, and validate how you recover
elements.label: Test recovery procedures

elements.description: Replace one large resource with many small ones, so no failure is shared by all
elements.label: Scale horizontally to increase aggregate workload availability

elements.description: Monitor demand and utilisation, and add or remove resources automatically
elements.label: Stop guessing capacity

elements.description: Make changes to infrastructure with automation, so they can be tracked and reviewed
elements.label: Manage change through automation

name: AWS - Performance Efficiency
description: The design principles of the Performance Efficiency pillar of the AWS Well-Architected Framework

elements.description: Use computing resources efficiently to meet requirements, and stay efficient as demand and technologies change
elements.label: Performance Efficiency

elements.description: Consume complex technologies as services, so teams focus on the product rather than running them
elements.label: Democratize advanced technologies

elements.description: Deploy in several Regions to give customers lower latency at minimal cost
elements.label: Go global in minutes

elements.description: Remove the need to run and maintain physical servers for traditional compute
elements.label: Use serverless architectures

elements.description: Virtual, automatable resources make it quick to compare instance, storage, or configuration types
elements.label: Experiment more often

elements.description: Use the technology approach that best fits how the data is accessed
elements.label: Consider mechanical sympathy

name: AWS - Cost Optimization
description: The design principles of the Cost Optimization pillar of the AWS Well-Architected Framework

elements.description: Run systems to deliver business value at the lowest price point
elements.label: Cost Optimization

elements.description: Invest in the capabilities, knowledge, and processes to become a cost-efficient organisation
elements.label: Implement cloud financial management

elements.description: Pay only for the computing resources you use, and scale them with business needs
elements.label: Adopt a consumption model

elements.description: Measure the business output of the workload and the costs of delivering it
elements.label: Measure overall efficiency

elements.description: Let AWS rack, stack, and power servers, so you focus on customers and projects
elements.label: Stop spending money on undifferentiated heavy lifting

elements.description: Identify the cost and usage of workloads and attribute them to their owners
elements.label: Analyze and attribute expenditure

name: AWS - Sustainability
description: The design principles of the Sustainability pillar of the AWS Well-Architected Framework

elements.description: Minimise the environmental impacts of running cloud workloads
elements.label: Sustainability

elements.description: Measure the impact of the workload and model its future impact
elements.label: Understand your impact

elements.description: Set long-term goals for each workload, and model the return on investment
elements.label: Establish sustainability goals

elements.description: Right-size workloads and remove idle resources for efficient use of energy
elements.label: Maximize utilization

elements.description: Design for flexibility, so efficient new technologies can be adopted quickly
elements.label: Anticipate and adopt new, more efficient hardware and software offerings

elements.description: Shared services across a broad customer base maximise resource utilisation
elements.label: Use managed services

elements.description: Reduce the energy or resources customers need to use your services
elements.label: Reduce the downstream impact of your cloud workloads
